svg.title: Rail-optimized Spectrum-X scalable unit: 32 DGX nodes × 8 SuperNICs = 8 rails
svg.text: Rail-optimized Spectrum-X scalable unit: 32 DGX nodes × 8 SuperNICs = 8 rails
NIC n of every node → leaf n. Same-rail NCCL traffic is one hop; cross-rail traffic uses spines with adaptive routing. 800G → 2×400G breakout on leaf downlinks
Each leaf: 16 × 800G uplinks (4 per spine) = 12.8 Tb/s up · 32 × 400G downlinks = 12.8 Tb/s down → non-blocking (1:1); 2:1 halves the uplinks
Orange: NIC 3 of every node lands on leaf03 (rail 3) — GPU 3 ↔ GPU 3 all-reduce never leaves the leaf. Grey: NIC 8 → leaf08, same rule.
Capacity math: 32 nodes × 8 NICs × 400G = 256 × 400G = 102.4 Tb/s of host bandwidth per SU, i.e. 128 × 800G leaf ports after breakout.
Spine count = uplinks per leaf for full ECMP spread; with AR the spines behave as one pooled layer so 2:1 stays usable for rail-local collectives.
Management and storage ride a separate conventional Ethernet network (not shown).
